title: Soviet-Afghan War
summary: Soviet troops invaded Afghanistan in late December 1979 to prop up the faltering communist government against mujahideen guerrillas. The war became a stalemate with large refugee flows, about 15,000 Soviet dead, and a Soviet withdrawal completed on 15 February 1989, leaving the guerrillas unbeaten.

as_recorded.value: The Soviet withdrawal was completed on February 15, 1989

where.modern_name: Afghanistan (proxy pin: Democratic Republic of Afghanistan, the location Wikidata lists)

importance.justification: Cold War superpower war that displaced millions and contributed to the Soviet Union's decline.

audience_note: Involves mass civilian death and displacement of refugees.
